query: What visit-note signals suggest a longer visit?

per_column.name: procedural_intervention_present
per_column.rationale: Whether a procedure, injection, biopsy, or medication change occurred is a distinct clinical activity that plausibly drives visit length without being a restatement or deterministic function of duration. Legitimate predictor knowable from the note.

per_column.name: diagnostic_workup_scope
per_column.rationale: Extent of labs/imaging ordering is a separate work-intensity signal that correlates with longer visits; it is not a component of duration itself and carries real predictive signal.

per_column.name: clinical_severity_level
per_column.rationale: Severity of the clinical picture is an independent covariate plausibly associated with longer, more complex visits. Not a restatement or leakage of duration.

per_column.name: emergency_critical_status
per_column.rationale: Emergency/critical escalation status is an external condition variable that plausibly influences visit length; not derived from duration.

per_column.name: specialist_consultation_or_referral
per_column.rationale: Consultation/referral involvement reflects added care coordination that can extend a visit; a distinct activity variable, not a restatement of duration.

per_column.name: counseling_education_complexity
per_column.rationale: Amount/type of counseling or education is a plausible time-consuming activity distinct from the duration measure; legitimate predictor.

per_column.name: comorbidity_or_multisystem_scope
per_column.rationale: Patient complexity/comorbidity burden is an independent covariate that plausibly predicts longer visits without leaking the outcome.

judge.rationale: All seven added columns capture distinct clinical-activity and complexity dimensions extractable from visit notes. Each lies outside the focus variable (visit_duration_min) -- none restates it, is a deterministic component of it, or is knowable only after the outcome in a leaking sense; they describe what happened during the visit, which is a legitimate driver of duration rather than a post-hoc measurement of it. As a set they cover complementary axes (procedures, diagnostics, severity, emergency status, referrals, counseling, comorbidity), giving substantial and non-redundant predictive leverage beyond the original department/urgency/age columns. Utility is high but not maximal because several dimensions correlate with one another and with the existing urgency column, and none directly quantifies time.
